mainTopic: The end of the מחלוקת between רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל about trusting a חבר to tithe, followed by the new משנה about placing an עירוב תחומין in a tree or a pit, and the opening question of the גמרא about where that tree stands.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא about a חבר who asked an עם הארץ to pick figs for him. רבי says a second חבר who overheard may eat the figs without tithing, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says he must tithe first. The גמרא explains the root of their disagreement: would a חבר do a small איסור himself to stop an עם הארץ from doing a big one? A new משנה then teaches that an עירוב placed in a tree is valid below ten טפחים but not above, and an עירוב in a pit is valid at any depth. The אמוראים ask where the tree stands, and they reject both a רשות היחיד and the simple versions of a רשות הרבים. They conclude that the tree stands in a רשות הרבים, the person rests below, and the משנה follows רבי, who holds that a rabbinic שבות does not apply during בין השמשות. רב נחמן confirms this in the name of שמואל, who adds that the tree is ten טפחים high and four wide. רבא limits the rule to a tree outside the city's outskirts, and the גמרא challenges him from his own four-אמות rule. רב יצחק בריה דרב משרשיא begins to answer that the tree leans out beyond four אמות, and his answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי says the second חבר may eat without tithing
steps.stepSummary: רבי rules that the second חבר may eat the figs without tithing, because the first חבר certainly tithed them already.
steps.simpleTranslation: [רבי] holds: that חבר may eat and does not need to tithe, because that first חבר certainly tithed the figs for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing רבי's opinion in the ברייתא: the חבר who overheard may eat the figs without tithing them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי assumes the first חבר would never let an עם הארץ eat untithed food (טבל). So the first חבר must have tithed the figs, even though he did it from produce that was not next to these figs.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who is trusted to be careful about tithes and purity

phrases.english: [Rabbi] holds: that chaver may eat
phrases.notes: The subject is רבי, named on the previous amud. 'That חבר' is the one who overheard.

phrases.english: and he does not need to tithe,
because he certainly tithed [it]
that first chaver, on his behalf.
phrases.notes: The first חבר tithed so the עם הארץ would not eat טבל.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָבַר: אוֹתוֹ חָבֵר אוֹכֵל וְאֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ לְעַשֵּׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a ברייתא that began on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The overhearing חבר may eat without tithing, since the first חבר surely tithed.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל requires tithing first
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagrees: the second חבר may not eat until he tithes, because a חבר would not tithe from produce that is not next to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: he may not eat until he tithes, because חברים are not suspected of separating תרומה from produce that is not adjacent.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the opposing view: the second חבר must tithe before eating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ideally, תרומה and מעשר should be taken from produce that is right next to the produce being fixed (מן המוקף). A careful חבר would not take it from far away, so we cannot assume the first חבר tithed the figs while they were still in the field.

keyTerms.meaning: From produce that is adjacent (right next to it)

phrases.english: And Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
he may not eat until he tithes,
because chaverim are not suspected
of separating [tithes] from produce that is not adjacent.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: לֹא יֹאכַל עַד שֶׁיְּעַשֵּׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposing opinion in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The second חבר must tithe before eating, because a חבר would not tithe from non-adjacent produce.

steps.title: רבי answers that a minor flaw is better than feeding טבל
steps.stepSummary: רבי replies that it is better for חברים to tithe from non-adjacent produce than to let an עם הארץ eat טבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said to him: It is better that חברים be suspected of separating from non-adjacent produce, and not feed עמי הארץ untithed food.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי pushes back against רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי agrees that taking from non-adjacent produce is not ideal. He argues that a חבר would still choose it, because the alternative is letting an עם הארץ eat טבל, which is much worse.

keyTerms.meaning: Untithed produce, which is forbidden to eat

phrases.english: And Rabbi said to him:
It is better that chaverim be suspected
of separating from non-adjacent produce
and they should not feed amei ha'aretz tevel.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי: מוּטָב שֶׁיֵּחָשְׁדוּ חֲבֵרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי rebuts the reasoning of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the assumption that a חבר would never tithe from non-adjacent produce.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It ignores that the alternative, letting an עם הארץ eat טבל, is far worse.

steps.title: What is the root of their disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what principle the two תנאים disagree about.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the principle underneath this מחלוקת. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides accept the same facts. The גמרא wants to find which value each תנא puts first.

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the ברייתא's מחלוקת.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying principle that divides רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

steps.title: Small sin for me or big sin for him
steps.stepSummary: רבי holds a חבר prefers to do a small איסור himself so an עם הארץ avoids a big one. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds a חבר prefers to avoid even a small איסור, even if the עם הארץ then does a big one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי holds: a חבר prefers to do a light prohibition himself so the עם הארץ will not do a severe one. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds: a חבר prefers that the עם הארץ do a severe prohibition, while he himself does not do even a light one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question: the disagreement is about whether a חבר would take on a small wrong to save another person from a big wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'small איסור' is tithing from non-adjacent produce. The 'big איסור' is eating טבל. רבי says the חבר cares about the other person and tithes anyway. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says the חבר guards his own conduct first, so we cannot assume he tithed.
steps.whatToRemember: The whole מחלוקת comes down to one question: would a careful person do a small wrong himself to stop someone else from doing a big wrong? רבי says yes. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says no.
steps.confusionAlert: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל does not say the עם הארץ's sin is unimportant. He is describing what a חבר would actually prefer, and that tells us whether we can assume the figs were tithed.

phrases.english: Rabbi holds:
it is preferable to a chaver
that he himself commit a light prohibition

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא לֶיעֱבֵד עַם הָאָרֶץ אִיסּוּרָא רַבָּה.
phrases.english: so that the am ha'aretz not commit a severe prohibition.
And Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel holds:
it is preferable to a chaver
that the am ha'aretz commit a severe prohibition,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִיהוּ אֲפִילּוּ אִיסּוּרָא קַלִּילָא לָא לֶיעֱבֵד.
phrases.english: while he himself not commit even a light prohibition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They disagree about whether a חבר would do a light איסור himself to prevent an עם הארץ's severe איסור.

steps.title: משנה: an עירוב placed in a tree
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that an עירוב placed in a tree above ten טפחים is not valid, and below ten טפחים it is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: MISHNAH: If he placed it in a tree, above ten טפחים, his עירוב is not an עירוב. Below ten טפחים, his עירוב is an עירוב.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches what happens when someone puts his עירוב תחומין in a tree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Height matters here: above ten טפחים the עירוב fails, and below ten it works. The משנה does not say which domain the tree stands in, and the גמרא will ask about that.

keyTerms.meaning: Ten handbreadths, a key height in the laws of domains
Here, an עירוב תחומין: food placed to set one's Shabbos base

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
If he placed it in a tree,
above ten handbreadths —
his eiruv is not a valid eiruv;
below ten handbreadths —
his eiruv is a valid eiruv.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה. It is not connected to the tithing discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עירוב in a tree above ten טפחים is invalid; below ten טפחים it is valid.

steps.title: משנה: an עירוב placed in a deep pit
steps.stepSummary: An עירוב placed in a pit is valid, even if the pit is one hundred אמות deep.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he placed it in a pit, even one hundred אמות deep, his עירוב is an עירוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a second case: an עירוב in a pit is valid no matter how deep the pit is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Depth does not ruin the עירוב the way height in a tree can. Even a very deep pit is fine.

phrases.english: If he placed it in a pit,
even if it is a hundred cubits deep —
his eiruv is a valid eiruv.

steps.triggerLanguage: נְתָנוֹ בְּבוֹר, אֲפִילּוּ עָמוֹק מֵאָה אַמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second case of the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עירוב in a pit is valid even at great depth.

steps.title: The scholars ask where the tree stands
steps.stepSummary: A group of אמוראים sit together and ask in which domain the tree of the משנה is standing.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: רבי חייא בר אבא sat, with רבי אסי and רבא בר נתן, and רב נחמן sat beside them. They sat and said: this tree, where does it stand?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a group of אמוראים asking which domain the tree is in. This sets up the analysis that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule for above and below ten טפחים only makes sense once we know the tree's domain. So the scholars begin by defining the case.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba sat,
and Rabbi Asi and Rava bar Natan,
and Rav Nachman sat beside them,
and they sat and said:
This tree, where does it stand?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא begins analyzing the משנה's tree case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which domain the tree in the משנה is located in.

steps.title: In a private domain, height should not matter
steps.stepSummary: If the tree is in a רשות היחיד, there should be no difference between above and below ten טפחים, because a רשות היחיד extends all the way up to the sky.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it stands in a רשות היחיד, what difference is it to me whether it is above or below? A רשות היחיד goes up to the sky.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first possibility and challenges it right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A רשות היחיד has no height limit, so everything above it is still the same domain. If the tree were in a רשות היחיד, the משנה's line between above and below ten טפחים would make no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a possibility to be tested)

phrases.english: If you say it stands in a private domain,

phrases.aramaic: מָה לִי לְמַעְלָה מָה לִי לְמַטָּה?
phrases.english: what difference is it to me, above or below?
A private domain rises up to the sky.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects the first possible answer to step 8's question.
steps.kashyaTarget: The possibility that the tree stands in a רשות היחיד.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A רשות היחיד goes up to the sky, so the משנה's difference between above and below ten טפחים could not apply there.

steps.title: If the tree is in the public domain, where does he intend to stay?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries placing the tree in a רשות הרבים and asks where the person means to make his Shabbos place. If he chooses up in the tree, he and his עירוב are in the same place, so the עירוב should be valid even above ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say the tree stands in the public domain. Then where does he intend to make his Shabbos place? If you say he intended to rest up above in the tree, then he and his עירוב are in one place, so the עירוב should be valid.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting a רשות היחיד in step 9, the גמרא tries a new option: the tree is in a רשות הרבים. It immediately runs into a problem with the first way of picturing the case, where the person is up in the tree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עירוב only works if the person could reach it during בין השמשות. If the person makes his Shabbos place up in the tree, he is right next to his עירוב, so he has no reaching problem at all. That means the משנה's rule that 'above ten is invalid' could not be explained this way.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a possibility that will be tested)
He and his עירוב are in the same place

phrases.english: Rather, say that it stands in the public domain.
Where does he intend to establish his Shabbos residence?
If you say that he intended to rest above (in the tree) —
then he and his eiruv are in one place.
phrases.notes: So the עירוב should be valid even above ten, which contradicts the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the רשות היחיד option was rejected, the גמרא tries a רשות הרבים and tests its first version.
steps.kashyaTarget: The option that the tree stands in a רשות הרבים and the person rests above
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the person and the עירוב are in the same place, the height of the עירוב should not matter, so the משנה's distinction is unexplained.

steps.title: If he stays below, he would have to use the tree
steps.stepSummary: The second version is that the person rests on the ground below. But then reaching the עירוב means using the tree, which is forbidden on Shabbos, so even below ten should be invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say he intended to rest down below. But then he is making use of the tree!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the other way of picturing the case, with the person on the ground below the tree. It challenges this version as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking something out of a tree counts as using the tree, and that is forbidden on Shabbos. If so, the person could not get his עירוב even when it is below ten. That would make the עירוב invalid in every case, so the משנה's rule that 'below ten is valid' is unexplained.

keyTerms.meaning: Making use of a tree (forbidden on Shabbos)

phrases.english: Rather, he intended to rest below —
but he is making use of the tree!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the second version of the רשות הרבים case after the first one failed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The version where the tree is in a רשות הרבים and the person rests below
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Getting the עירוב requires using the tree, which is forbidden, so the עירוב should be invalid even below ten.

steps.title: He rests below, and the משנה follows רבי on twilight
steps.stepSummary: The tree really is in a רשות הרבים and the person rests below. The משנה follows רבי, who holds that rabbinic prohibitions (שבות) were not decreed for בין השמשות, so using the tree is allowed at that time.
steps.simpleTranslation: Actually, the tree stands in the public domain and he intended to rest below. This משנה follows רבי, who said: anything forbidden only because of a rabbinic שבות was not decreed during בין השמשות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 11. It keeps the case of the person resting below and explains why using the tree is not a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עירוב takes effect during בין השמשות. Using a tree is only a rabbinic שבות, and according to רבי that kind of prohibition does not apply at that time. So an עירוב below ten is reachable and valid. Above ten, the tree counts as a רשות היחיד, and bringing the עירוב down into the רשות הרבים would be Torah-level carrying, so it stays invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually / in truth (we keep the earlier assumption)
Twilight, the time of doubt between day and night

steps.confusionAlert: The עירוב is not invalid above ten because of using the tree. It is invalid because removing it would be Torah-level carrying from a רשות היחיד to a רשות הרבים. רבי's leniency only covers rabbinic prohibitions.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer explains both halves of the משנה at once by separating a rabbinic problem (using the tree) from a Torah problem (carrying between domains).

phrases.english: Actually, it stands in the public domain,
and he intended to rest below.
And it is according to Rebbi, who said:
anything that is forbidden only due to a rabbinic decree
they did not decree it during twilight.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about using the tree.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the משנה to a specific תנא (רבי)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Using the tree would forbid taking the עירוב, so even below ten would be invalid.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי, a שבות does not apply during בין השמשות. So below ten is valid, and above ten is invalid because of Torah-level carrying.

steps.title: רב נחמן approves and cites שמואל
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן tells the group that their explanation is correct and that שמואל said the same thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to them: Well said, and שמואל said the same.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן confirms the answer that the sitting אמוראים reached in step 12.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds outside support to the answer: it matches an earlier teaching of שמואל. That makes the explanation more than a guess.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא, a student of שמואל

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said to them:
Well said, and so said Shmuel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms the answer of step 12.
steps.raayaObject: The explanation that the tree is in a רשות הרבים and the משנה follows רבי

steps.title: Did you really go so far in explaining it?
steps.stepSummary: The scholars react with surprise and ask רב נחמן whether he and his colleagues worked out such a detailed explanation.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Did you explain it this far?!
steps.whatsHappening: The scholars (Sefaria: the חכמים of ארץ ישראל) respond to רב נחמן with an exclamation of surprise. This sets up the גמרא's next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They seem amazed that such a long, step-by-step explanation was worked out. Their reaction will be questioned in the next step.

phrases.english: They said to him:
Did you explain it this far?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A reaction to רב נחמן's statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רב נחמן's group really explained the משנה in such depth

steps.title: Why be surprised if they explained it the same way?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why they were surprised, since they themselves explained the משנה the same way.
steps.simpleTranslation: But they too explain it this way!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of step 14. Their surprise makes no sense if they held the same explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person does not express amazement at an explanation he already agrees with. So the words 'did you explain it this far' cannot be what they really meant.

phrases.aramaic: אִינְהוּ נָמֵי הָכִי קָא פָּתְרִי בָּהּ!
phrases.english: They too explain it this way!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינְהוּ נָמֵי הָכִי קָא פָּתְרִי בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of the question in step 14.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: They held the same explanation, so being surprised by it makes no sense.

steps.title: They asked whether it was fixed in their learning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rewords the question: they were asking whether this explanation was firmly set in their regular study. רב נחמן answered yes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what they said to him: Did you fix this in your learning? He said to them: Yes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own challenge by rewording what the scholars actually asked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They were not surprised by the idea itself. They wanted to know whether it was an established teaching passed down in the study hall. רב נחמן confirms that it was.

phrases.english: Rather, this is what they said to him:
Did you establish it in your learning?
He said to them: Yes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 15 by rewording the question.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: They were surprised at the explanation itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: They asked whether it was an established teaching, and רב נחמן said yes.

steps.title: שמואל's statement was explicitly recorded
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes שמואל's recorded teaching: the tree is in a רשות הרבים, ten טפחים high and four wide, the person rests below, and the משנה follows רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also stated: רב נחמן said in the name of שמואל: We are dealing with a tree standing in the public domain, ten טפחים high and four wide, and he intended to rest below. This follows רבי, who said that anything forbidden only as a שבות was not decreed during בין השמשות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the formal recorded version of שמואל's teaching, which backs up רב נחמן's 'yes'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל adds that the tree is ten טפחים high and four wide. That size makes the upper part of the tree a רשות היחיד. This explains why bringing the עירוב down from above ten would be Torah-level carrying.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also stated (introduces a recorded teaching)
Ten טפחים high and four wide, the size of a רשות היחיד

steps.whatToRemember: The tree is a רשות היחיד standing in a רשות הרבים, and the person rests below. Below ten, only a rabbinic שבות is involved, which רבי permits during בין השמשות, so the עירוב is valid. Above ten, getting it means Torah-level carrying, so it is invalid.

phrases.english: It was also stated:
Rav Nachman said that Shmuel said:

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא בָּאִילָן הָעוֹמֵד בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים עָסְקִינַן,
phrases.english: Here we are dealing with a tree standing in the public domain,
ten handbreadths high and four wide,
and he intended to rest below,
and it is according to Rebbi, who said:
anything that is forbidden only due to a rabbinic decree
they did not decree it during twilight.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִתְּמַר נָמֵי, אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב נחמן's 'yes' with שמואל's recorded statement.
steps.raayaObject: The explanation of the משנה's tree case
steps.raayaSupportSource: A recorded teaching of רב נחמן in the name of שמואל

steps.title: רבא limits the law to trees outside the city outskirts
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the משנה only refers to a tree outside the outskirts of the city. Inside the outskirts, even an עירוב above ten is valid, because a city is treated as if it were filled in.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: They only taught this about a tree standing outside the outskirts of the city. But for a tree standing inside the city's outskirts, even above ten it is a valid עירוב, because a city is viewed as if it were filled in.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a new limit to the משנה's rule: it only applies outside the city's outskirts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Inside a city and its outskirts, we picture the ground as raised up to the height of the עירוב. So the person and the עירוב count as being in one place. For that reason, the above-ten problem does not arise there.

keyTerms.meaning: The outskirts of the city (about 70⅔ אמות around it)

steps.whyThisMatters: The משנה's rule about ten טפחים applies only in open areas outside a city, not in every location.

phrases.english: Rava said:
They taught this only regarding a tree
standing outside the outskirts of the city,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אִילָן הָעוֹמֵד בְּתוֹךְ עִיבּוּרָהּ שֶׁל עִיר —
phrases.english: but a tree standing within the outskirts of the city —

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ לְמַעְלָה מֵעֲשָׂרָה הֲרֵי זֶה עֵירוּב,
phrases.english: even above ten, it is a valid eiruv,
because a city is considered as though filled in.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the case is defined, רבא limits where the rule applies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עירוב in a tree above ten is invalid only outside the city's outskirts. Inside them, it is valid, because a city is viewed as if filled in.

steps.title: רבא's own four-cubits rule should make height irrelevant everywhere
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא: by his own rule, the four אמות around the עירוב count as a רשות היחיד, which reaches the sky. So even outside the outskirts, an עירוב above ten טפחים should be fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then outside the outskirts of a city too there should be no problem. Since רבא said that one who places his עירוב has four אמות, that area becomes a רשות היחיד, and a רשות היחיד goes up to the sky!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's limit from Step 18 by quoting another teaching of רבא himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said a city counts as 'filled in,' so height does not matter inside the outskirts. But רבא also said the person gets four אמות around his עירוב, and those count as a רשות היחיד. Since a רשות היחיד has no height limit, the tree's upper parts should count as private outside the city as well, so רבא's limit seems to fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (a common opening for a challenge)
The outskirts of a city, the area just around it that is treated as part of the city
Four cubits, the small personal area a person is given
Rises up to the sky, meaning it has no height limit

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not quoting a new rabbi against רבא. It is pointing to a different teaching of רבא himself and arguing that his two teachings do not fit together.

phrases.english: If so,
outside the outskirts of a city also [it should be valid],
since Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: הַנּוֹתֵן עֵירוּבוֹ יֵשׁ לוֹ אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת,
phrases.english: one who places his eruv has four cubits,
phrases.notes: The person is treated as if he lives at the spot of the עירוב, and he gets four אמות there.

phrases.english: it becomes a private domain
and a private domain rises up to the sky!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, חוּץ לְעִיבּוּרָהּ שֶׁל עִיר נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's distinction between inside and outside the outskirts in Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that outside the outskirts, an עירוב above ten טפחים is invalid
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא's own rule gives the person four אמות that count as a רשות היחיד. A רשות היחיד reaches the sky, so height should never matter, even outside the city.

steps.title: The case is a tree leaning beyond four cubits
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בריה דרב משרשיא answers that the משנה is talking about a tree whose branches stretch out past four אמות from its trunk. The answer continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק, the son of רב משרשיא, said: Here we are dealing with a tree that leans out beyond four אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יצחק בריה דרב משרשיא starts to defend רבא by narrowing the case to a tree that leans far to the side. The sentence is not finished, and the rest of his answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge only works if the עירוב is inside the person's four-אמות private area. By saying the tree leans past four אמות, he moves the עירוב (as the Sefaria translation explains) outside that area. Then the 'rises to the sky' rule no longer covers it, and height matters again.

keyTerms.meaning: A tree that leans or bends to the side
We are dealing with (used to narrow the case)

steps.whyThisMatters: This answer keeps רבא's two teachings working together by placing the case outside the four-אמות private area.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא:
phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak son of Rav Mesharshiya said:
here, with a tree that leans
beyond four cubits we are dealing,
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא בָּאִילָן הַנּוֹטֶה חוּץ לְאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 19 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא) to a specific physical setup
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed the עירוב was on the tree inside the person's four אמות, which would make it private all the way up.
steps.terutzMaskana: The tree leans out past four אמות, so the spot of the עירוב is outside the private four-אמות area. Height therefore still matters outside the outskirts.
